statement: Total nonfarm payroll employment fell by 23,000 in July 2026.
usage_note: Single-month estimate is not statistically different from zero at BLS's 90 percent threshold; use with corroboration.

statement: The unemployment rate was 4.1 percent in July.
usage_note: CPS estimate; changed little over the year.

statement: May payroll growth was revised from 129,000 to 63,000.
usage_note: Additional establishment reports and recalculated seasonal factors.

statement: June payroll growth was revised from 57,000 to 20,000.
usage_note: June can be revised again with the August report.

statement: May and June payrolls combined were 103,000 lower than previously reported.
usage_note: Use to show that the August 7 information shock included history.

statement: The latest May-July average payroll change was 20,000 per month.
BLS said payroll growth averaged 34,000 per month over the prior twelve months before the July change.
usage_note: BLS's stated prior-twelve-month average; not a film-package recomputation.

statement: Private payrolls rose by 30,000 in July.
usage_note: Total payroll decline also reflects government losses.

statement: Government payrolls fell by 53,000 in July.
usage_note: Local government education accounted for most of the estimate.

statement: The civilian labor force fell by 264,000 in July to 169.094 million.
units_and_adjustment: thousands month over month; seasonally adjusted
usage_note: Do not infer every exiting person's prior status or reason.

statement: Household employment fell by 87,000 in July to 162.177 million.
units_and_adjustment: thousands month over month; seasonally adjusted
usage_note: CPS monthly sampling uncertainty is large.

statement: The number unemployed fell by 178,000 in July to 6.916 million.
units_and_adjustment: thousands month over month; seasonally adjusted
usage_note: Explains the rate arithmetic together with the smaller labor force.

statement: The number outside the labor force rose by 381,000 in July.
units_and_adjustment: thousands month over month; seasonally adjusted
usage_note: Stock change does not identify individual flows or motives.

statement: Labor-force participation was 61.4 percent in July and was 0.7 point lower than in January.
units_and_adjustment: percentage point change; July level 61.4; seasonally adjusted
usage_note: January-July comparison is after the January population-control break.

statement: The employment-population ratio was 58.9 percent in July and was 0.5 point lower than in January.
units_and_adjustment: percentage point change; July level 58.9; seasonally adjusted
usage_note: BLS explicitly highlighted the since-January decline.

statement: U-6 labor underutilization was 7.9 percent in July, unchanged from July 2025.
usage_note: Includes marginal attachment and part-time for economic reasons.

statement: Long-term unemployment was 1.771 million and 25.5 percent of all unemployment.
units_and_adjustment: percent share; level 1.771 million; seasonally adjusted
usage_note: Shows persistent hardship despite low current layoff flow.

statement: Temporary layoffs rose 153,000 to 921,000 while permanent job losers were little changed near 1.7 million.
usage_note: Do not generalize the temporary-layoff increase into a broad firing wave.

statement: Average hourly earnings were $37.62 and rose 3.2 percent over the year.
units_and_adjustment: percent year over year; nominal; seasonally adjusted level
usage_note: Average can be affected by workforce composition; cross-check ECI.

statement: The private average workweek was 34.3 hours and the aggregate weekly-hours index was unchanged in July.
usage_note: Supports absence of labor-input growth in July.

statement: Local government education payrolls fell by about 50,000 in July.
usage_note: BLS says the sector had little net change over the prior twelve months.

statement: Retail trade payrolls fell by about 19,000 in July.
usage_note: General merchandise and fuel retail were weak; selected hobby and miscellaneous retail rose.

statement: Financial-activities payrolls fell by 14,000 in July and were down 121,000 from the May 2025 peak.
units_and_adjustment: thousands from peak; July monthly change -14,000
usage_note: Employment does not mechanically measure credit supply or profitability.

statement: Health-care payrolls rose by 22,000 in July, slower than their 36,000 trailing-twelve-month average.
usage_note: Ambulatory health-care services accounted for about 18,000.

statement: Health-care payrolls rose by about 391,900 from July 2025 to July 2026.
usage_note: Use latest same-vintage levels and preserve retrieval date.

statement: Total payrolls rose 316,000 year over year, so payrolls outside health care fell about 75,900.
units_and_adjustment: thousands; calculated as total minus health care
official_source: BLS CES total and health-care series
usage_note: Valid statement is all other sectors combined; not that every other sector shrank.

statement: The private-sector employment diffusion index was 51.8 in July; manufacturing was 50.0.
usage_note: Counterweight to a generalized-collapse thesis.

statement: From February to July the concept-adjusted household employment series fell 563,000 while CES payrolls rose 422,000.
usage_note: CPS remains noisier and adjustment is incomplete; index series for presentation.

statement: January 2026 population controls lowered estimated labor force and employment by about 1.4 million each, participation by 0.4 point, and EPOP by 0.5 point; the unemployment rate was essentially unaffected.
units_and_adjustment: thousands level effect; rate effects in percentage points
usage_note: Do not treat December-January level discontinuity as economic movement.

statement: Job openings were 7.359 million with a 4.4 percent rate in June.
usage_note: Openings are a last-business-day stock and lag July payrolls.

statement: Hires were 5.348 million with a 3.4 percent rate in June.
units_and_adjustment: percent rate; 5.348 million level; seasonally adjusted
usage_note: Below the February 2020 hire rate of 3.9 percent.

statement: Quits were 3.232 million with a 2.0 percent rate in June.
units_and_adjustment: percent rate; 3.232 million level; seasonally adjusted
usage_note: Below the February 2020 quit rate of 2.3 percent.

statement: Layoffs and discharges were 1.766 million with a 1.1 percent rate in June.
units_and_adjustment: percent rate; 1.766 million level; seasonally adjusted
usage_note: Below the February 2020 rate of 1.3 percent.

statement: There were about 1.04 June job openings per June unemployed person.
usage_note: Descriptive balance measure only; ignores skill, wage, geography, and timing mismatch.

statement: Initial unemployment-insurance claims were 209,000 in the week ended August 8, versus 224,000 in the comparable 2025 week.
official_source: U.S. Department of Labor weekly claims
usage_note: Strong check against a broad layoff wave; excludes ineligible and nonfiling job losers.

statement: Insured unemployment was 1.777 million in the week ended August 1, versus 1.942 million a year earlier.
official_source: U.S. Department of Labor weekly claims
usage_note: Insured unemployment rate was 1.2 percent versus 1.3 percent a year earlier.

statement: Civilian compensation rose 0.9 percent in Q2 and 3.4 percent over the year.
units_and_adjustment: percent year over year; 0.9 percent q/q seasonally adjusted
usage_note: Do not compare SA quarterly rate directly with NSA twelve-month rate.

statement: Private-industry wages rose 3.1 percent over the year.
units_and_adjustment: percent year over year; not seasonally adjusted
usage_note: Composition-controlled corroboration of 3.2 percent AHE growth.

statement: Private benefits rose 3.8 percent over the year and private health benefits rose 6.0 percent.
usage_note: Benefits were rising faster than wages.

statement: All-employee real average hourly earnings fell 0.2 percent from July 2025 to July 2026.
units_and_adjustment: percent year over year; CPI-U deflated
usage_note: Real weekly earnings rose 0.1 percent because weekly hours were slightly higher.

statement: CPI-U rose 0.1 percent in July and 3.4 percent over the year; core CPI rose 2.5 percent over the year.
units_and_adjustment: percent year over year; seasonally adjusted monthly change
usage_note: Energy was up 14.7 percent y/y; distinguish headline from core.

statement: Nonfarm-business productivity rose at a 1.4 percent annual rate in Q2 and 2.2 percent over the year.
units_and_adjustment: percent year over year; q/q SA annual rate 1.4
usage_note: Residual and revision-prone; does not identify AI as cause.

statement: Nonfarm-business output rose 2.5 percent year over year while hours rose only 0.2 percent.
usage_note: Core evidence for output-without-hours interpretation.

statement: Unit labor costs rose 1.3 percent annualized in Q2 and 1.4 percent over the year.
units_and_adjustment: percent year over year; q/q SA annual rate 1.3
usage_note: Can be margin-supportive but is not a profit measure.

statement: The preliminary labor-share estimate was 52.9 percent, the lowest in the series beginning in 1947.
usage_note: Striking secondary fact; do not make it the central thesis before revision.

statement: Real GDP grew at a 1.5 percent annualized rate in Q2 after 2.1 percent in Q1.
units_and_adjustment: percent q/q seasonally adjusted annual rate
usage_note: Second estimate due August 26.

statement: Real final sales to private domestic purchasers grew at a 3.9 percent annualized rate in Q2 after 1.7 percent in Q1.
units_and_adjustment: percent q/q seasonally adjusted annual rate
usage_note: Private demand counterweight to labor weakness.

statement: June real personal consumption rose 0.4 percent and the personal saving rate was 2.7 percent.
units_and_adjustment: percent saving rate; real PCE m/m 0.4 percent
usage_note: Predates July and aggregate saving masks distribution.

statement: July retail and food-service sales fell 0.6 percent from June and rose 5.0 percent from a year earlier.
units_and_adjustment: percent m/m; seasonally adjusted; nominal; +/-0.4 point 90 percent margin
usage_note: Not price adjusted; not all consumption; cannot prove a consumption recession.

statement: Total business applications rose 8.1 percent in July to 578,926.
usage_note: Retail applications rose 44.5 percent and heavily influenced the headline.

statement: High-propensity business applications rose 1.4 percent while applications indicating planned wages fell 1.6 percent.
usage_note: Applications are not operating businesses or payroll jobs.

statement: Projected employer formations within four quarters rose 0.7 percent to 29,959.
units_and_adjustment: percent m/m; seasonally adjusted model projection
usage_note: Projection is hiring-adjacent but not an observed job count.

statement: The FOMC held the federal-funds target at 3.50 to 3.75 percent on July 29 by a 9-3 vote.
usage_note: The decision predates the August 7 July jobs report.

statement: Three FOMC voters preferred a 25-basis-point rate increase on July 29.
usage_note: Evidence against an automatic weak-jobs-equals-immediate-cuts narrative.

statement: The July Beige Book reported five districts with employment gains and seven with little or no change.
usage_note: Contact anecdotes; explicitly not the views of Federal Reserve officials.

statement: The July 29 FOMC statement and press conference preceded the August 7 Employment Situation.
usage_note: Do not claim the Fed's July language incorporated the later payroll print or revisions.

statement: BLS scheduled the preliminary March 2026 CES benchmark revision for August 28 and the final benchmark for February 2027.
usage_note: Rerun payroll-level claims after publication; preliminary does not immediately revise official history.

statement: BLS's approximate 90 percent significance thresholds are 122,000 for a one-month total-payroll change and 650,000 for a one-month household-employment change.
usage_note: Use trends and triangulation; do not overread individual monthly point estimates.
